moduleTitle: Advanced Use Cases - Module Properties for Realistic Interaction
learningObjectives: Define and configure Module properties to enhance mobile automation.
Explain how Module properties change the way a control is identified and steered.
Use properties to make automated interaction behave more like real user interaction.
Recognise which flaky-step problems are solved at Module level rather than in the TestCase.

elements.term: Fix it once, not in every TestCase
elements.description: A Module describes a control: how to find it and how to interact with it. Every TestCase that steers that control inherits the description. So a property adjusted on the Module applies everywhere the control is used, while the same adjustment made inside a TestCase applies to that TestCase alone. When the same control misbehaves across several TestCases, the Module is the correct place to fix it, and fixing it in each TestCase instead is how a workaround gets copied twenty times.

elements.text: A useful test for where a fix belongs: if the answer to 'why is this step configured this way' is a fact about the control, it belongs on the Module. If it is a fact about this particular scenario, it belongs in the TestCase.

bulletPoints: Module properties describe the control and apply everywhere it is used.
Fact about the control goes on the Module. Fact about the scenario goes in the TestCase.

elements.description: A scan captures several properties per control and selects some of them to identify it. That automatic selection is a starting point rather than a verdict. Properties that look stable in one scan can turn out to be dynamic in practice, such as text that is localised, an index that shifts when a list reorders, or a coordinate that moves with screen size. Editing which properties participate in identification is how a Module is made resilient without touching a single TestCase.

elements.title: Signals that identification needs adjusting
items: A step fails only in another language, which points at localised text being used to identify.
A step fails only when a list has a different number of items, which points at index-based identification.
A step fails only on a different screen size, which points at coordinates carrying identification weight.
A step fails only after an unrelated UI change nearby, which points at identification depending on surrounding structure.

elements.text: Each of those failures reproduces reliably under one specific condition and passes everywhere else, which is exactly why they are usually blamed on the environment rather than on identification. The condition under which a step fails is normally the clearest available evidence of which property is doing the identifying.

bulletPoints: Automatic property selection during a scan is a starting point, not a final answer.
The condition under which a step fails usually names the unstable property.

elements.description: A framework can often set a value directly on a control, which is fast and reliable and completely unlike what a user does. Mobile UIs frequently attach behaviour to the interaction itself rather than to the resulting value: validation that runs on blur, a picker that only commits on confirm, a list that lazy-loads as it scrolls, an animation that has to finish before the next control accepts input. Automation that sets values directly can bypass all of that, which produces a TestCase that passes while the user-facing flow is broken.

elements.title: Interaction behaviours worth configuring at Module level
items: Scrolling a control into view before interacting, rather than assuming it is on screen.
Tapping to focus before entering text, so focus-dependent behaviour actually fires.
Respecting keyboard behaviour after text entry, so the keyboard does not cover the next target.
Allowing animations or transitions to settle before the next interaction is attempted.

elements.text: The general point: a test that passes by taking a shortcut the user cannot take has quietly stopped testing the thing you meant to test. Configuring interaction to resemble real use is not only about stability, it is about the result still meaning something.

bulletPoints: Mobile behaviour often hangs off the interaction, not off the final value.
Setting values directly can produce a green TestCase over a broken user flow.

examPitfalls.title: Working around a control's behaviour in every TestCase
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Adding the same wait, scroll, or extra tap in each TestCase that touches a particular control.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If the adjustment is a fact about the control rather than about one scenario, configure it on the Module so every TestCase inherits it. Repeating it per TestCase multiplies the maintenance and guarantees inconsistency.

examPitfalls.title: Trusting the scan's automatic identification unconditionally
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming the properties chosen during scanning are stable, then treating the resulting condition-specific failures as environment problems.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Read the condition under which the step fails. Failing only in another language, only at a different list length, or only on a different screen size each point directly at which property is unstable, and the fix is to change what identifies the control.

examPitfalls.title: Setting values directly instead of interacting realistically
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Writing a value straight into a control and getting a green TestCase, while the real flow depends on focus, confirmation, or scroll-triggered loading.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure interaction to match how the control is genuinely used when behaviour is attached to the interaction. A TestCase that bypasses that behaviour can pass over a user-facing defect.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The same control needs an extra scroll before it can be interacted with, and it is used across eleven TestCases. Where does that adjustment belong?

options.text: In each of the eleven TestCases, so the intent stays visible locally.
On the Module, since the need to scroll is a fact about the control rather than about one scenario.
In a TCP at Project level.
It cannot be configured and must be handled with an image-based control.

practiceQuiz.hint: Ask whether the reason is about the control or about the scenario.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The requirement follows the control everywhere it is used, so it belongs on the Module where every TestCase inherits it. Repeating it in eleven TestCases multiplies maintenance and invites inconsistency.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A step works in English and fails when the same build runs with the app set to German. What does this most directly indicate?

options.text: Localised text is participating in how the control is identified.

practiceQuiz.hint: The one thing that changed between the passing and failing run was the language.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A failure that reproduces only under a language change points at localised text being used for identification. The fix is to change which properties identify the control rather than to treat it as an environment issue.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why can setting a value directly on a mobile control produce a passing TestCase over a broken user flow?

options.text: Direct value setting is not supported on Android.
Mobile behaviour is often attached to the interaction itself, such as validation on blur or a picker that commits only on confirm, and setting the value bypasses it.
It always triggers an Appium session restart.
Values set directly are discarded when the keyboard closes.

practiceQuiz.hint: Consider what fires on focus, blur, confirm, or scroll that a direct write skips.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When behaviour hangs off the interaction rather than the resulting value, bypassing the interaction skips validation, commit steps, and lazy loading. The TestCase then verifies a path the user cannot take.

quickRecap.value: Module properties describe the control and apply to every TestCase that uses it.
Fact about the control goes on the Module. Fact about the scenario goes in the TestCase.
Scan-selected properties are a starting point. Adjust which properties identify the control when they turn out to be dynamic.
Fails only in another language means localised text. Only at a different list length means index. Only on another screen size means coordinates.
Scroll into view, tap to focus, manage the keyboard, let animations settle. Behaviour attached to the interaction is skipped by a direct value write.
